title: The President Tried to Pull the Cameras Off Her.

brand.cta: Follow The Black History Room for one story a day.

beats.text: The President tried to pull cameras off her.

overlays.hook: The President tried *to pull cameras off her.*

beats.text: The youngest of twenty children of Mississippi sharecroppers, she picked cotton from age six.
In 1962, she tried to register to vote. That night, she was thrown off the plantation where she worked.
In 1963, in a Winona jail, police ordered two Black prisoners to beat her with a blackjack.
In 1964, her Freedom Democratic Party challenged Mississippi's all-white delegation at the Democratic convention.

visual.caption: Freedom Democratic Party supporters, Atlantic City, August 1964

beats.text: On live television, she told the committee everything.

visual.caption: The Credentials Committee, Atlantic City, August 22, 1964

beats.text: President Johnson called a sudden press conference, to pull the cameras away from her.
It didn't work. That night, the networks aired her testimony anyway.
Is this America, she asked, the land of the free and the home of the brave?
She died in 1977. Her gravestone reads: I am sick and tired of being sick and tired.

facts.claim: Born 6 Oct 1917, youngest of 20 children of sharecroppers; picked cotton from age 6.
Aug 1962 tried to register; the plantation owner told her to withdraw or leave; she left that night.
June 1963, Winona jail: patrolmen ordered two Black prisoners to beat her with a blackjack; lasting injuries.
1964 MFDP challenge to the all-white regular delegation at the Democratic National Convention.
Testified to the Credentials Committee, 22 Aug 1964, televised.
Johnson called an impromptu press conference during her testimony to divert attention.
The networks broadcast her testimony later (that evening).
'Is this America, the land of the free and the home of the brave...'
Died 14 March 1977; gravestone: 'I am sick and tired of being sick and tired.'
